items.title: Section: The Abode Joined With Dependent Origination Opens — Ten Kinds of Equality Among All Dharmas

items.zh: 云何菩薩緣起相應增上慧住？謂諸菩薩，先於諸諦相應增上慧住，已得十種法平等性當知文詞如經廣說。
items.en:
Seventh abode, joined with dependent origination; first, the question. What is a bodhisattva's abode joined with dependent origination?
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, entry brought to fulfilment through the equality of ten dharmas; first, pointing to what the sutra says. Namely, bodhisattvas, previously at the abode joined with the truths, have already attained ten kinds of equality among dharmas; the wording follows exactly as the sutra explains at length.
Commentary: Regarding "ten kinds of equality among dharmas" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: if a bodhisattva, having well accomplished the path of the fifth ground, wishes to enter the sixth bodhisattva ground, should enter by ten kinds of equal dharma. What are the ten? First, the equality of all dharmas being without mark. Second, being without conception. Third, being unarisen. Fourth, being unaccomplished. Fifth, being quiescent. Sixth, being originally pure. Seventh, being free of conceptual proliferation. Eighth, being free of grasping and rejecting. Ninth, being like an illusion, a dream, a shadow, an echo, the moon in water, a reflection in a mirror, a mirage, and a conjured apparition. Tenth, being neither existent nor non-existent. The treatise explains each individually; this should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Entry Confirmed, and All Ten Equalities Unpacked in Full — Closing the First Aspect

items.zh: 如是十種法平等性成上品故，極圓滿故，超過前住得入此住。謂於一切法，由有勝義自性無相平等性故；言說造作影像無相平等性故；即由此相自然不生平等性故；因亦不生平等性故；自然與因皆不生故，畢竟本寂平等性故；現有體事能取正智，離諸戲論平等性故；遠離一切取捨造作平等性故；即此煩惱眾苦雜染離繫解脫平等性故；分別所執境界自性如幻化等平等性故；無分別智所行自性有無無二平等性故。當知是名此中十種法平等性略分別義。
items.en:
Second, clarifying entry. These ten kinds of equality among dharmas, becoming of the most excellent grade, utterly complete, cause one to pass beyond the previous abode and enter this one.
Third, clarifying the brief meaning. Regarding all dharmas: by their own nature possessing ultimate truth, they are equally without mark; being mere images constructed through speech, they are equally without conception; by this very markless nature, they naturally do not arise, equally; their cause, too, does not arise, equally; because neither their own nature nor their cause arises, they are, in the final analysis, originally quiescent, equally; though appearing to possess substantial matters, the wisdom genuinely grasping this is free of conceptual proliferation, equally; entirely departed from every grasping and rejecting, equally; the very afflictive suffering that defiles is equal to the very liberation that unbinds; the nature of whatever object discriminating attachment grasps is illusion-like, equally; and the very sphere non-discriminating wisdom operates within is, in its own nature, without duality between existence and non-existence, equally. One should understand this as the brief, distinguishing meaning of these ten kinds of equality among dharmas here.

items.title: Section: Awakening to Dependent Origination Gives Rise to the Three Gates of Liberation — Emptiness, Signlessness, Wishlessness

items.zh: 如是菩薩住此住中，於諸有情增長悲愍；於大菩提生起猛利欲樂悕求；於諸世間合散生滅，以一切種緣起正觀觀察了知。依緣起智，能引發空、無相、無願三解脫門。
items.en:
Second aspect: awakening to dependent origination, giving rise to the gates of liberation. Such a bodhisattva, abiding in this abode, increases compassion towards sentient beings; arouses intense eagerness and longing for great awakening; and, regarding the world's own coming-together and dispersing, arising and ceasing, correctly observes and genuinely understands this through every kind of correct contemplation of dependent origination. Relying on this wisdom of dependent origination, one is able to draw forth the three gates of liberation: emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
Commentary: Regarding "the world's own coming-together and dispersing, arising and ceasing" — a sentient being's own embodied existence is called the world. Affliction's own binding conditions converging is called coming-together, and from this coming-together, birth occurs. Should those same afflictive conditions be broken apart, this is called dispersing, and from this dispersing, permanent cessation occurs. Regarding all of this, observing forward and backward through the links of dependent origination, one attains genuine wisdom — this is called correct contemplation of dependent origination through every kind. Because one observes the two kinds of selflessness through dependent origination, one is thereby able to draw forth the gate of emptiness. Because one observes each link, one by one, brought to cessation, one is thereby able to draw forth the gate of signlessness. Because one observes this cyclic flow generating no wish to remain, except solely for great compassion's refusal to abandon sentient beings, one is thereby able to draw forth the gate of wishlessness. These gates of liberation belong exclusively to what is world-transcending, as explained individually in the Compendium Establishing the Teaching, one should understand.

items.title: Section: No Notion of Self or Other, Agent or Patient, Existence or Non-Existence Ever Arises Again

items.zh: 由是因緣，所有自他、作者、受者、有無等想，皆不復轉。
items.en:
Third aspect: every wrongful notion no longer manifests. By this cause and condition, every notion of self and other, of agent and patient, and of existence and non-existence entirely ceases to turn.
Commentary: Regarding "by this cause and condition" and the like — the sutra says a bodhisattva practising the three gates of liberation thereby departs from the mark of self, departs from the mark of agent and patient, and departs from the mark of existence and non-existence. These three departures, in their proper order, have the three gates of liberation as their own cause and condition; this is why it is said in this way here.

items.title: Section: Neither Contaminated by Saṃsāra Nor Abandoning It — Consciousness Itself Not Defiling, Yet Defiled

items.zh: 菩薩如是善於勝義顧念有情，如理通達煩惱繫故，緣和合故，有為諸法自性羸劣。離我我所無量過失污染而轉；非離一切煩惱繫縛，眾緣和合。是故我今為自防護，應令一切煩惱繫縛、眾緣和合皆悉斷壞；為益有情，不應永滅一切有為。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: regarding sentient beings with genuine care, taking up saṃsāra for their sake. Such a bodhisattva, skilled in ultimate truth, regards sentient beings with genuine care. Genuinely penetrating that conditioned dharmas, bound by affliction and arising through the coming-together of conditions, are by their own nature weak and dependent. Free of self and what belongs to self, yet turning under countless afflictive faults; not otherwise arising apart from affliction's binding and the coming-together of conditions.
Commentary: Regarding "conditioned dharmas are by their own nature weak and dependent" — form and non-form aggregates are called conditioned dharmas. Each has its own particular generating cause, called its own nature. Unable to arise by itself, awaiting further conditions to arise — this is called weak. Furthermore, consciousness's own nature cannot defile another, and yet is defiled by another — this too is called weak. One should thereby understand that conditioned dharmas turn under countless afflictive faults solely through affliction's own binding and the coming-together of conditions, not through any self or what belongs to self actually doing anything, since self and what belongs to self have no real nature at all.
Therefore I should now guard myself, causing every affliction's binding and every coming-together of conditions to be entirely broken apart and destroyed. Yet, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, I should not permanently extinguish all conditioned existence.

items.title: Section: Unattached Wisdom Directly Present — Neither Existence Nor Non-Existence, the Non-Dual Wisdom Opens

items.zh: 如是菩薩住此住中，智悲隨逐，名無著智現前、般若波羅蜜多住現前。
items.en:
Fifth aspect: unattached wisdom's own abiding directly manifest; first, naming it. Such a bodhisattva, abiding in this abode, wisdom and compassion following one another closely, is named as one in whom unattached wisdom is directly present, and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom is directly present.
Commentary: Regarding "named as one in whom unattached wisdom is directly present" — this refers to directly realising that saṃsāra and nirvana are equal, thereby attaining non-dual wisdom.

items.title: Section: Three Marks of Unattached Wisdom — Undefiled by the World, Sharp Forbearance, Abiding in Neither Extreme

items.zh: 由此住故，於一切世間行無染而行。又即此住有猛利忍。於第七地有加行行邊際菩薩忍，當知是彼隨順忍攝。又此無著智現前、般若波羅蜜多住現前，能引能引菩提眾緣，於諸世間有為諸行住而不住；雖於寂滅見寂靜德，而亦不住。
items.en:
Second, explaining the marks; first, undefiled by the world. Because of dwelling in this abode, one acts amid every kind of worldly activity without any defilement whatsoever.
Second, possessing sharp forbearance. This same abode also possesses sharp forbearance. Regarding the seventh ground's own applied-effort boundary bodhisattva-forbearance, one should understand this sixth-ground forbearance as subsumed within its accordant cause.
Third, abiding in neither extreme. This unattached wisdom directly present, and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom directly present, are able to draw forth every condition contributing to awakening. Towards every conditioned activity in the world, one abides without truly abiding; although beholding quiescence's own peaceful virtue, one likewise does not abide there.
Commentary: Regarding "able to draw forth every condition contributing to awakening" — the factors of awakening are able to fulfil the great fruit of awakening; this is called drawing forth every condition contributing to awakening. Now, unattached wisdom directly present and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom directly present are able to draw forth every one of the factors of awakening; this is why it is said, drawing forth every condition contributing to awakening.

items.title: Section: Immeasurable Absorption — Hundreds and Thousands of Gates Into Emptiness, Wishlessness, and Signlessness

items.zh: 如是菩薩方便般若智所隨逐，能入空三摩地，令十百千上首三摩地門皆現在前。如空三摩地，如是無願、無相三摩地，當知亦爾。
items.en:
Sixth aspect: realising immeasurable absorption; first, citing the absorption of emptiness. Such a bodhisattva, followed closely by skilful means and wisdom, is able to enter the absorption of emptiness, causing ten, a hundred, a thousand foremost gates of absorption all to become directly present.
Second, extending by example to wishlessness and signlessness. Exactly as with the absorption of emptiness, one should understand that entering the absorptions of wishlessness and signlessness proceeds in just the same way.
Commentary: Regarding "causing ten, a hundred, a thousand foremost gates of absorption" — the sutra says ten kinds of emptiness-absorption gates serve as the foremost, a hundred thousand myriad emptiness-absorption gates all becoming directly present. This should be explained accordingly. Below, it says signlessness and wishlessness each further possess their own ten as foremost, exactly as the sutra explains, one should understand.

items.title: Section: Nine Kinds of Unshakeable Aspiration — From Unshakeable Faith to a Mind Fully Satisfied With Skilful Means

items.zh: 由此上首三摩地門現在前故，意樂不壞。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: realising unshakeable aspiration. Because these foremost gates of absorption are now directly present, aspiration itself becomes unshakeable.
Commentary: Regarding "aspiration becomes unshakeable" — this means that aspiration is firm and does not regress; this is called unshakeable. This has nine distinct kinds, exactly as the sutra explains, one should understand.

items.title: Section: Demonic Forces and Rival Teachings Cannot Wrest Away This Sovereign Mastery

items.zh: 於一切種諸佛聖教，一切外道及諸魔軍、聖教怨敵，不能引奪。
items.en: Eighth aspect: demonic and hostile forces unable to wrest it away. Regarding every kind of the buddhas' own noble teaching, every non-Buddhist path, every kind of demonic force, and every hostile power opposed to the noble teaching, are entirely unable to seize or wrest it away.

items.title: Section: Gold Now Set With Lapis Lazuli, and Wisdom Like Moonlight No Wind of the Four Seasons Can Extinguish

items.zh: 餘如前說。此差別者，謂如世間善巧工匠，以所鍊金作莊嚴具，琉璃寶珠瑩飾廁鈿，一切餘金不能映奪。如是此中菩薩善根清淨殊勝，如先所說不能映奪。又如月光，於有情身能令悅豫，非四風輪所能斷壞。如是此中菩薩慧光，一切有情煩惱欝蒸皆能息滅，一切外道、魔軍、怨敵不能斷壞。
items.en:
Ninth aspect: purified wholesome roots; first, the general account; first, pointing to what was already said. Everything else follows exactly as already explained.
Second, a simile marking the difference. The difference is this: just as, in the world, a skilful craftsman's own smelted gold, wrought into an ornament and set with lapis lazuli for brilliant adornment, cannot be equaled by any other gold lacking such adornment — so too this bodhisattva's own purified, excellent wholesome roots, exactly as already described, cannot be outshone.
Second, a further simile specifically for the faculty of wisdom. Just as moonlight brings genuine delight to sentient beings' own bodies, and cannot be broken apart by any of the four wheels of wind — so too this bodhisattva's own wisdom-light is able to extinguish the oppressive, stifling heat of affliction in every sentient being, and cannot be broken apart by any non-Buddhist teaching, demonic force, or hostile power.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as Lord of the Heaven of Manifest Delight, and Threefold Majestic Power Reaching a Hundred Thousand Koṭi

items.zh: 受生多作妙化天王，善化有情，令除一切增上慢等。所有威力，當知此中說百千俱胝數。
items.en:
Tenth aspect: rebirth. Taking rebirth, one most often becomes the lord of the Heaven of Manifest Delight, skilfully transforming sentient beings, causing them to eliminate every kind of spiritual overconfidence and comparable fault.
Eleventh aspect: majestic power. One should understand that the majestic power spoken of here reaches a hundred thousand koṭi.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Eleven Aspects, and the Treatise Confirms — This Is the Ground of Direct Presence

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩緣起相應增上慧住。謂十法平等性成滿得入故；覺悟緣起生解脫門故；一切邪想不現行故；方便攝受生死故；無著智現前、般若波羅蜜多住現在前故；證得無量三摩地故；證得不壞意樂故；於佛聖教不可引奪故；廣見諸佛、善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經現前地說。由此地中，無著智現前、般若波羅蜜多住現在前故，名現前地。即由此義，當知亦名緣起相應增上慧住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode joined with dependent origination — namely, because entry is brought to fulfilment through the equality of ten dharmas; because awakening to dependent origination gives rise to the gates of liberation; because every wrongful notion no longer manifests; because saṃsāra is skilfully taken up for beings' sake; because unattached wisdom and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom are directly present; because immeasurable absorption is realised; because unshakeable aspiration is realised; because nothing can wrest away mastery of the buddhas' own noble teaching; because of broadly beholding the buddhas and purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of direct presence.
Second, explaining. Within this ground, because unattached wisdom and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom are both directly present, this ground is named the ground of direct presence.
Third, the correspondence. By this very meaning, one should understand this is also named the abode joined with dependent origination.

blocks.text: On the sixth ground, dependent origination is seen so clearly that the ideas of self and other, doer and receiver, simply stop arising.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the name tells us this ground takes dependent origination as its object. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the sixth ground, "Directly Present".
Master Cháng Bǎi: chant Amitābha into an empty valley and it chants back, but no one is there; like a rabbit conjured by a magician. Venerable Miào Jìng: like an image in a mirror.

Master Cháng Bǎi: following origination forward brings birth and death; in reverse it accords with nirvāṇa. Venerable Miào Jìng: without existence there is no birth; without birth, no ageing and death.

"Every notion of self and other, agent and patient, existence and nonexistence ceases." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I'm sitting in meditation": the meditator cannot be found. "It's hot": the one who feels cannot be found.

Master Cháng Bǎi: beings and the world arise only with conditions, hence weak; they cannot stain others but are stained by others. Venerable Miào Jìng: affliction is a villain, and the mind does many evil things together with it.
Venerable Miào Jìng: this is fundamental wisdom, clinging to no dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are equal; free of all marks, non-dual wisdom is realised.
Venerable Miào Jìng: skilful-means wisdom is subsequent wisdom; prajñā is fundamental wisdom.
Venerable Miào Jìng: samādhi protects the aspiration. Master Cháng Bǎi: the power of calm and insight is a pillar supporting the path to buddhahood.

Master Cháng Bǎi: lapis is worth more than agate. Both lecturers: the four winds that cannot dim this wisdom are the four demons: spring's gentle wind the demon of afflictions, summer's the aggregates, autumn's death, winter's the god-demon.
"Because unattached wisdom and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom are present, it is called the Manifest Ground." Master Cháng Bǎi: abiding neither in saṃsāra nor in nirvāṇa.
Try Venerable Miào Jìng's exercise: when you next think "I'm hot" or "I'm tired", look for the one who feels it.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi characterise the object of contemplation at the sixth ground?
options: the name shows the bodhisattva here takes dependent origination as the object
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing "dependent origination" in the name, we know the bodhisattva here takes dependent origination as the object. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the sixth ground, Manifest.

quiz.q: For "images constructed by speech are equally markless," what examples does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: chanting Amitābha into an empty valley — it echoes back, but no one is there; like a magician's rabbit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: chant Amitābha into an empty valley and it chants back, but no one is there; like a rabbit conjured by a magician. Venerable Miào Jìng: like an image in a mirror — not real.

quiz.q: "Relying on the wisdom of dependent origination, the three gates of liberation are drawn forth." What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: forward origination yields suffering, reverse accords with nirvāṇa; seeing the flow, no wish arises for it; Miào Jìng: no existence, no birth; no birth, no ageing and death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: following origination forward brings the fruit of birth and death; in reverse it accords with nirvāṇa; observing the flow, no wish for it arises. Venerable Miào Jìng: without existence there is no birth; without birth no ageing and death.

quiz.q: After the three gates, which notions cease?
options: self and other, agent and patient, existence and nonexistence
quiz.why: "Every notion of self and other, agent and patient, existence and nonexistence ceases." Venerable Miào Jìng: "I'm sitting in meditation" — the meditator is unfindable; "it's hot" — the one who feels is unfindable.

quiz.q: "Conditioned dharmas are weak by nature." How do the lectures explain "weak"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: unable to arise alone, needing conditions, and stained by others — hence weak; Miào Jìng: affliction is a villain, and the mind joins it in evil
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: beings and the world cannot arise by themselves, only with conditions — hence weak; they can't stain others but are stained by others. Venerable Miào Jìng: affliction is a villain, and the mind does many evil things together with it.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain "unattached wisdom directly present"?
options: Miào Jìng: it is fundamental wisdom, clinging to nothing; Cháng Bǎi: saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are equal, realising non-dual wisdom free of all marks
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "unattached wisdom directly present" is fundamental wisdom, clinging to no dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are equal; free of all marks, non-dual wisdom is realised.

quiz.q: "Followed by skilful-means wisdom and prajñā, entering emptiness absorption." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the two?
options: skilful-means wisdom is subsequent wisdom, prajñā fundamental wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: skilful-means wisdom is subsequent wisdom; prajñā is fundamental wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: tens, hundreds, thousands of samādhi gates appear, emptiness foremost.

quiz.q: "Because these samādhi gates are present, aspiration is unshakeable." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the link?
options: samādhi protects the aspiration; with concentration and wisdom guarding, compassion and wisdom aren't lost
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: samādhi protects the aspiration; protected by concentration and wisdom, compassion and wisdom are not lost. Master Cháng Bǎi: the power of calm and insight is a pillar supporting the path to buddhahood.

quiz.q: In the sixth ground's simile, what adorns the gold?
quiz.why: "Gold wrought into an ornament and set with lapis lazuli." Master Cháng Bǎi: lapis is worth more than agate, and gleams brilliantly.

quiz.q: "Moonlight that the four winds cannot destroy." How do the lectures map the four winds?
options: both: spring's gentle wind is the demon of afflictions, summer's the aggregates, autumn's death, winter's the god-demon
quiz.why: Both lecturers: spring's gentle wind is the demon of afflictions, summer's bright wind the aggregates, autumn's cool wind death, winter's cold wind the god-demon.

quiz.q: What is the sixth abode called in the Ten Grounds Sūtra, and why?
options: Manifest — unattached wisdom and the perfection of wisdom are present
quiz.why: "Because unattached wisdom and the abiding of the perfection of wisdom are present, it is called the Manifest Ground." Master Cháng Bǎi: abiding neither in saṃsāra nor nirvāṇa, compassion and wisdom together.
